active_learning.evidence: Session is mostly student MCQ attempts with brief tutor explanations, but many turns are empty or stalled (turns 85, 87, 89, 91).

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Tutor generally follows explanations with an MCQ (e.g., turn 72, 76), though some turns are empty (85, 87) breaking the flow.

deliberate_practice.evidence: On repeated errors at 360-190, tutor cycles through similar MCQs rather than a clean varied retry; some scaffolding (turn 76) is reasonable but turn 78 introduces a confusing 200-based decomposition.

mastery_learning.evidence: Tutor moves on from 360-190 once student gets 170 (turn 80) but never re-checks the original 'third angle' question; also the 60÷5 sub-skill is being drilled without diagnosing place-value bottleneck.

cognitive_load.evidence: Turn 78's '360-200=160, add 10 back' reasoning is awkward and high-load for an error-prone S3 student; figure references appear without an inline figure (turn 68).

layering.evidence: Tutor links new problem (5 equal angles) to the 360° total, and breaks 360÷5 into 300÷5 + 60÷5, leveraging prerequisite division facts.

non_interference.evidence: 180° (straight line) vs 360° (point) are explicitly contrasted in turn 68/70; no confusable topics back-to-back.

interleaving.evidence: Problems stay narrowly on 360-sum subtraction/division; no genuine mixing of problem types.

testing_effect.evidence: Tutor poses MCQs before explaining (turn 66, 72), giving genuine retrieval attempts, though hints sometimes come too eagerly (turn 76).

targeted_remediation.evidence: When student repeatedly fails 360-190 and 60÷5, tutor recycles the same MCQ (turns 74, 97, 99) rather than diagnosing the place-value or subtraction prerequisite.

strongest_behaviors: Explicit contrast between 180° (straight line) and 360° (point) when correcting the first error (turn 68/70).
weakest_behaviors: Multiple empty tutor turns (85, 87, 89, 91) that derail the session and force the student to self-tutor.
Recycling identical MCQs after wrong answers (turns 74, 97, 99) instead of remediating the prerequisite skill.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid empty tutor turns
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Several tutor turns are entirely empty, causing the student to take over the tutoring role.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Every tutor turn MUST contain at least one sentence of feedback AND either a question or a clearly marked next step. Never emit an empty message.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates stalled turns and keeps tutor in control of the dialogue.

prompt_recommendations.title: Ban verbatim MCQ recycling on wrong answer
prompt_recommendations.rationale: After wrong answers the tutor often re-posts the identical MCQ with no new scaffold, which doesn't help an error-prone student.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: If 30 divided by 5 is 6, what is 300 divided by 5? A) 50 B) 60 C) 70 D) 80
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'If a student answers an MCQ incorrectly, do NOT repost the same options. Provide a new scaffold (worked sub-step, simpler analogous problem, or place-value breakdown) before re-asking.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces genuine remediation instead of guess-cycling.

prompt_recommendations.title: Diagnose prerequisite on repeated failure
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student repeatedly fails simple subtraction/division; tutor should branch to a prerequisite check rather than persist.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'After two consecutive errors on the same micro-skill, switch to a prerequisite diagnostic (e.g., single-digit subtraction or 10x place-value) before returning to the target problem.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Targets the actual bottleneck instead of looping.

prompt_recommendations.title: Don't reference figures that aren't shown
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor refers to 'the diagram' but no figure is rendered inline, increasing load.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Look at the diagram to see how many degrees make up
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Only reference a diagram if you are emitting one inline in the same turn. Otherwise describe the visual in words.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Removes dangling figure references that confuse the student.

prompt_recommendations.title: Avoid convoluted decomposition strategies
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 78's '360-200=160, then add 10 back' is more confusing than direct subtraction.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: If you have 360 and take away 200, you have 160 left. Since 190 is 10 less than 200, we add that 10 back to 160.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Prefer the simplest decomposition (e.g., 360-190 = 360-200+10 stated as a single step, or column subtraction). Avoid multi-step reasoning that itself requires the skill being remediated.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Lowers cognitive load for error-prone students.

prompt_recommendations.title: Close the original question before moving on
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student's original question 'what is the third angle?' was never explicitly answered as 170°; tutor pivoted to a new problem.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Spot on—you'd have 170 sweets! That's exactly right, which means 360 - 190 = 170.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'After solving a sub-step, explicitly restate the answer to the original question before introducing a new problem.'

flow_recommendations.title: Detect and retry empty model outputs
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine emitted multiple empty tutor turns; orchestration should retry or fall back.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents student from having to drive the lesson.

flow_recommendations.title: Cap consecutive wrong answers before prerequisite routing
flow_recommendations.rationale: Student missed the same subtraction question 3+ times with no routing to a prereq lesson.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Triggers prereq remediation automatically after N failures.

flow_recommendations.title: Role-confusion guard
flow_recommendations.rationale: Because tutor turns were empty, the student began producing tutor-style replies; engine should detect role inversion.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: You're close! You divided 360 by 6, but there are five equal angles.

experience_recommendations.title: Inline visual for angles around a point
experience_recommendations.rationale: An error-prone S3 student would benefit from a labelled diagram showing 90°, 100°, and the unknown angle.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Look at the diagram to see how many degrees make up

experience_recommendations.title: Warmer tone after repeated errors
experience_recommendations.rationale: After 3+ wrong attempts, encouragement and a 'let's slow down' beat would help an error-prone learner.

overall_summary: The tutor opens reasonably with a clear contrast between 180° and 360°, but the session deteriorates: multiple empty tutor turns force the student into the tutor role, and on repeated arithmetic errors the tutor recycles identical MCQs rather than diagnosing the prerequisite subtraction/division skills. Targeted remediation, mastery gating, and cognitive-load management are the weakest areas. Highest-priority fixes are forbidding empty turns, banning verbatim MCQ recycling, and routing to prereq diagnostics after consecutive failures.
